articles.title: Defense reporters reject Chinese's embassy swipe at Filipino journalists
articles.summary: The Defense Press Corps rejected remarks made by the Chinese Embassy in Manila against Filipino journalists, whom it said have “very limited comprehension” and are only “creating hype.”

blocks.text: Published October 19, 2026 12:29am

The Defense Press Corps (DPC) on Sunday rejected remarks made by the Chinese Embassy in Manila against Filipino journalists, whom it said have “very limited comprehension” and are only “creating hype.”
The Chinese Embassy issued the statement after reports quoted Ambassador Jing Quan as saying that while China could easily win if it used force against the Philippines, it chooses peace instead.
“Some Philippine politicians and reporters have very limited comprehension about facts,” the Chinese Embassy Manila wrote on Facebook.
“But they are good at exaggeration, taking things out of context, and creating hype,” it added.

The DPC—the reporters on the defense beat—pointed out that reports of the Chinese Ambassador’s statement about choosing peace were reported verbatim, and its “political fallout is neither within the control nor the responsibility of journalists.”
It added that Filipino reporters consistently practice balanced reporting by always seeking the Chinese side’s response to every issue.
“Filipino reporters regularly sail and fly over the West Philippine Sea, where they have witnessed and experienced Chinese aggression at sea,” the DPC said.

“At the same time, we have consistently sought the Chinese side’s response to every issue, including water cannon attacks, collisions, and new remarks from Philippine government officials, in the spirit of fair play and balanced reporting,” it added.

The group also emphasized the challenge of operating without a free press, and noted the provisions under Article 2 of the United Nations Charter, which obliges states to refrain from using force and to settle disputes by peaceful means.

“Let us remember that under Article 2 of the United Nations Charter, states are obliged to refrain from the threat or use of force against the territorial integrity or political independence of any state, and to settle international disputes by peaceful means,” the DPC said.
The group added that reaching true peace takes mutual understanding—something that won't happen if China keeps “shooting at the messengers.” — BM, GMA News

articles.title: Meloni backs police after cost-of-living protests turn violent in Italian cities
articles.summary: Anger over living costs and low wages has brought Italians onto the streets. A major union has called a general strike for November 20.

image.caption: Clashes broke out in Milan during demonstrations against high living costs and low wagesImage: Stefano Porta/LaPresse/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni on Sunday condemned rioting during cost-of-living protests, expressing solidarity with police after clashes in several cities.
The violence broke out during cost-of-living demonstrations on Saturday, leaving at least four police officers and 20 demonstrators injured in Milan.
The unrest comes amid anger over high prices, stagnant real wages and a shortage of affordable housing in major cities.
What happened during the protests?
In Milan, black-clad, masked youths threw fireworks and bottles at police and erected barricades in the central Piazza Duomo, the Italian news agency ANSA reported.
Police initially withdrew to await reinforcements and later used tear gas to clear the square. Some 50 young people were arrested, about half of them minors, according to ANSA.
Clashes also broke out in Turin, Bologna and Bergamo. Police in Bologna used water cannon and made four arrests, all minors, with seven people reported to prosecutors.
How did Italy's PM Meloni respond?
Meloni expressed solidarity with police on Sunday, condemning criminals who she said exploited demonstrations to provoke confrontations and "sow chaos."
Italy tightens restrictions on the right to protest
"Demonstrating is a right, but setting our cities on fire is not," she said.
Milan Mayor Giuseppe Sala also condemned the violence while acknowledging the grievances behind the demonstrations.
"The reasons for the protest were understandable. The violence against police and the serious damage to the city, however, cannot be justified," he said.
Why were people demonstrating?
Protesters rallied against high living costs and low wages, with households facing expensive fuel and difficulty finding affordable housing.
In Rome, thousands joined a demonstration organized by the Italian General Confederation of Labour (CGIL). Its leader, Maurizio Landini, announced a general strike for November 20.
The violence came as similar demonstrations in France descended into rioting, arson and looting, with more than 1,800 people arrested nationwide.

articles.title: China taking advantage of VP impeachment raps?
articles.summary: The Chinese ambassador’s provocative remarks against the Philippine government and its officials may actually be a ploy of Beijing to create more internal political havoc on the highly divisive…

blocks.text: Headlines
October 19, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The Chinese ambassador’s provocative remarks against the Philippine government and its officials may actually be a ploy of Beijing to create more internal political havoc on the highly divisive impeachment issue of Vice President Sara Duterte, according to a former lawmaker.

“Is China simply pursuing its aggressive maritime agenda, or is it also taking advantage of our political divisions to weaken our resolve? These are questions our national security officials must examine,” former Surigao del Norte congressman Robert Ace Barbers said.

The House of Representatives’ impeachment adviser also stressed that while timing alone does not prove a deliberate connection, the possibility that China could “exploit domestic political tensions to advance its strategic interests cannot be dismissed without proper scrutiny.”
“The impeachment proceedings are an internal constitutional process. China has no business exploiting our political differences to advance its interests in our waters,” Barbers said.

He warned that a nation preoccupied with internal political battles risks losing focus on external threats. China could benefit if the impeachment controversy deepens divisions among Filipinos and distracts the public from developments in the West Philippine Sea (WPS).
From the administration’s perspective, Duterte has been very lenient and is actually pro-China.

Barbers said the government must determine whether the timing and patterns of Chinese activities point to a broader strategy. Any assessment, he emphasized, must be supported by credible intelligence and verifiable evidence – not political speculation.

He urged Filipinos, regardless of political allegiance, to remain vigilant against possible foreign interference and resist efforts to turn domestic disagreements into national vulnerabilities, like the highly sensitive issue of China’s encroachment into the WPS.

“Whether coincidence or calculated strategy, China’s actions demand scrutiny. We may disagree on politics, but defending our sovereignty and protecting our national interests must unite us all,” Barbers said.
As far as Rep. Leila de Lima is concerned, Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan’s statement basically says “we are stronger, so be grateful that we don’t use our might to crush you.”

“This is absolutely the language of a liar and an invader who lacks sincerity in promoting peace. They may be mightier, but the world knows who has already won in our fight for sovereign rights over the WPS. And they know the consequences if they resort to using force against us,” De Lima said.

“If they truly love peace, then they should get out of our territory and stop harassing our countrymen and depriving our fishermen of their livelihoods. They are the ones encroaching on our territory,” the former senator and justice secretary pointed out.

“But being a bully, China will not stop threatening us. We will also keep defending what is ours. They cannot threaten us, because we Filipinos will never ever allow ourselves to be oppressed, conquered or subjugated,” De Lima said.

articles.title: DENR expands watershed repairs, forest protection vs El Niño
articles.summary: The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) has stepped up its mitigation efforts on watershed restoration and forest protection to address water supply concerns amid El Niño.

blocks.text: October 19, 2026 | 12:00am
People visit the Pililla Wind Farm in Rizal yesterday. The 54-megawatt wind farm features 27 wind turbines that generate renewable electricity for the Luzon grid.
Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) has stepped up its mitigation efforts on watershed restoration and forest protection to address water supply concerns amid El Niño.

The DENR said it is expanding forest protection patrols and accelerating targeted reforestation across critical watersheds nationwide to help forests retain water, regulate streamflow, reduce soil erosion and recharge depleted aquifers.
The effort combines the restoration of degraded and fire-damaged areas with measures to keep newly planted trees alive and protect existing forests.

DENR chief Juan Miguel Cuna said the DENR is mobilizing local communities, civil society groups, Indigenous Cultural Communities and field personnel to maintain forest cover and strengthen the natural systems that support water security.
In Central Luzon, DENR is carrying out forest restoration activities across critical watersheds in Aurora, Bataan, Nueva Ecija and Zambales.

In Nueva Ecija, the Manila Bay Site Coordinating and Management Office is inspecting established narra plantations to assess seedling survival rates and soil moisture conditions under elevated heat indices.
In the Bicol region, DENR offices are combining new tree-growing activities with measures to improve the survival of existing plantations.

In Masbate, the Provincial Environment and Natural Resources Office partnered with the Integrated Bar of the Philippines Bicol Chapter, local government units and the Community Environment and Natural Resources Office to plant more than 16,750 indigenous and mangrove seedlings across 50 hectares in the province’s second and third districts.

In Camarines Norte, DENR field officers require contractors under the Enhanced National Greening Program to establish plantations to replace dead seedlings and follow supplemental watering schedules to improve the tree survival under dry conditions.
In the Caraga region, field units are prioritizing the rehabilitation of fire-affected peatlands, riverbanks and protected areas.

Protecting existing watersheds is also essential to securing water supplies, as in Davao City, the Apo Agua Infrastructura Inc. and the Obu-Manuvu Indigenous Cultural Community conducted a comprehensive habitat assessment of the Panigan-Tamugan Sub-watershed, which serves as the city’s primary source of potable water.

In another development, the Department of Labor and Employment is preparing advisories on workplace safety during El Niño, with measures meant to protect workers from extreme heat without cutting their pay.
Senseless remedy
The Alliance of Concerned Teachers yesterday called the decision of the Department of Education to allow students to wear sleeveless shirts as a “senseless remedy” to the effects of super El Niño.

In a statement, ACT chairperson Ruby Bernardo said the Marcos administration and DepEd are resorting to superficial measures instead of addressing the systemic neglect that leaves public schools ill-equipped to withstand extreme weather and climate-related hazards. — Delon Porcalla, Christine Boton, Evelyn Macairan

articles.title: ‘Stop pitting President Marcos vs VP Sara’
articles.summary: President Marcos has his hands full and is simply beyond comparison with Vice President Sara Duterte, who is just waiting for the former to be incapacitated, for her to take over the reins of…

blocks.text: October 19, 2026 | 12:00am
President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. and Vice President Sara Duterte on January 25, 2024.
STAR / KJ Rosales

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos has his hands full and is simply beyond comparison with Vice President Sara Duterte, who is just waiting for the former to be incapacitated, for her to take over the reins of government, a former congressman said over the weekend.

“President BBM (Bongbong Marcos) has a whole lot of different responsibilities compared to the VP. It is like comparing apples and oranges. The President is the only one in charge of making day to day decisions, both popular and unpopular,” former Surigao del Norte 2nd District representative Robert Ace Barbers said.

As things stand in the governmental hierarchy, Duterte “discharges no official duties that carry responsibilities nor make or break the government,” Barbers said. “So, you see, they are of different characters.”
Barbers cautioned the public to be critical and more circumspect in analyzing information including those that fan the flames of discord and without any meaningful objective.

articles.title: Evidence on dropped impeachment raps going to ombudsman
articles.summary: Documentary and testimonial evidence against Vice President Sara Duterte on the three impeachment charges House prosecutors have dropped will be turned over to the ombudsman for possible prosecution…

blocks.text: October 19, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Documentary and testimonial evidence against Vice President Sara Duterte on the three impeachment charges House prosecutors have dropped will be turned over to the ombudsman for possible prosecution of criminal offenses.

Manila 3rd district Rep. Joel Chua over the weekend said they would comply with the call of Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla for the turnover of all the necessary evidence, hinting this may even involve non-bailable plunder charges based on the P612.5-million confidential funds alone.

“To begin with, this involves P612.5 million. This simply is too high from the threshold of plunder (which is P50 million). Aside from this, of course, there is also the possible charge of malversation (of public funds), and so forth and so on,” he pointed out during a weekly news forum over the weekend.

Malversation of public funds involves the unlawful appropriation, taking or misuse of public funds or property other than for its original purpose by an accountable public officer, requiring probers to establish the specific acts and circumstances supporting the alleged infraction.

The alleged reckless use of confidential funds from the Office of the Vice President and the Department of Education is among the three charges that prosecutors have dropped, along with grave threats and direct bribery of education officials.

Duterte in November 2024 threatened to have President Marcos, First Lady Liza Marcos and former speaker Martin Romualdez killed if she herself would be assassinated.This was after her chief of staff Zuleika Lopez was held in contempt and held at the House of Representatives.

“To put into perspective: it doesn’t necessarily mean that when we dropped the articles, the VP will already be free from any accountability. This will of course continue in other ways, like through the criminal proceedings (in the ombudsman),” Chua stressed.
Layman’s terms
The defense, on the other hand, is looking to simplify the discussion on the remaining Article of Impeachment, which is expected to be numbers-heavy.

“I think if there is anything we would like to do in our presentation, we would like to laymanize things and maybe simplify things to be able to understand it better, because in many of these things, you just need to show logic. If we can establish that, without going into the technicalities, that is something that we look forward to doing,” defense spokesman Michael Poa said in an interview over radio dzMM.
Poa did not disclose the number of witnesses that the defense would present, but it is expected that they would have their own financial expert.

articles.title: MBC hopes impeachment trial over by year-end
articles.summary: Business group Makati Business Club (MBC) has expressed support for concluding the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte within the year to allow the Senate to thoroughly review the budget…

blocks.text: October 19, 2026 | 12:00am
The Senate impeachment court opens oral arguments on requests to subpoena the financial records of Vice President Sara Duterte on July 15, 2026.
Senate Social Media Unit / Wendell Alinea

MANILA, Philippines — Business group Makati Business Club (MBC) has expressed support for concluding the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte within the year to allow the Senate to thoroughly review the budget that will support economic growth next year.
Edgar Chua, chairman of the MBC, told reporters that the group is hopeful the impeachment trial would not drag on to 2027.
“It’s a distraction. Our Senate should be doing a lot like the budget,” he said.

He said the Senate should review the proposed 2027 budget passed by the House of Representatives, citing concerns on realigned funds from education, health and transportation toward short-term social assistance.
“That’s wrong because that’s patronage politics,” he said.
He also said that more funds are needed to support the education, health and transportation sectors.
While MBC wants the impeachment proceedings to wrap up within the year, the group also wants to ensure it is done fairly.

With less than two years left in the current administration, he said that the 2027 budget would play a critical role in driving meaningful economic growth, hence the need to closely monitor how it will be spent.
Economic growth slowed to 2.3 percent in the second quarter, the weakest in five years.
From January to June, average economic growth was at 2.6 percent, below the government’s 3.5 to 4.5 percent growth target.
While the country’s slower economic growth is attributed to the Middle East crisis and high cost of goods, Chua said that the slower government spending is also a factor.
The tighter screening of infrastructure projects following the flood control controversy last year has led to slower government infrastructure spending.
“A big component of economic growth is government spending,” Chua said.
While infrastructure spending needs to accelerate, he also said this should be done right.
Presently, the Senate impeachment court is on break as senators focus on deliberations of the proposed 2027 budget. It will resume proceedings on Nov. 9.

articles.title: Chinese embassy: Persona non grata threat an old trick
articles.summary: The Chinese embassy in Manila warned that anyone who tries to provoke China will be “pushed back,” as it challenged politicians moving to declare its top diplomat in the country persona…

blocks.text: October 19, 2026 | 12:00am

“Some anti-China politicians talked about declaring the Chinese ambassador persona non grata (PNG). Over the past 30 years, anti-China forces have been repeatedly doing the same thing to threaten our embassy.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — The Chinese embassy in Manila warned that anyone who tries to provoke China will be “pushed back,” as it challenged politicians moving to declare its top diplomat in the country persona non grata to “do it quickly and immediately.”

“Some anti-China politicians talked about declaring the Chinese ambassador persona non grata (PNG). Over the past 30 years, anti-China forces have been repeatedly doing the same thing to threaten our embassy. We are fed up with these old and low tricks. If they really want to do something, do it quickly and immediately, please,” the embassy said in a Facebook post.
“While diplomacy is based on reciprocity. We will not welcome them to China. Simple and fair enough,” it said.
The embassy also accused Sen. JV Ejercito of bluffing, describing it as a typical political performance of a Philippine politician filled with conceit and arrogance.

“Make no mistake: respect is mutual. China treats all countries as equals, big or small, but will never tolerate ill-intentioned remarks, smears or provocations. As representatives of China, the Embassy will firmly safeguard China’s sovereignty, security, and dignity,” the embassy said.
“Anyone who tries to provoke China will be pushed back. We have never talked down to anyone. Yet the despicable conduct of those anti-China politicians truly invites contempt,” it added.
The behavior of anti-China politicians, the embassy said, is “utterly disgraceful.”
On Saturday, the embassy also castigated the Philippine media for having “very limited comprehension about facts.”

blocks.text: October 19, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Navy launched its third offshore patrol vessel, the future BRP Rajah Humabon, in Ulsan, South Korea, as part of its modernization program, the Navy said yesterday.
Navy flag officer-in-command Vice Admiral Jose Ma. Ambrosio Ezpeleta and Armed Forces of the Philippines vice chief of staff Lt. Gen. Rommel Roldan witnessed the launching ceremony on Oct. 13.

Built by South Korean shipbuilder HD Hyundai Heavy Industries, the Rajah Humabon is expected to strengthen the Navy’s maritime surveillance, maritime security, and territorial defense capabilities. It was named after the 16th-century ruler of Cebu when Portuguese explorer Ferdinand Magellan arrived in 1521.

Ahead of the ceremony, Ezpeleta met with Republic of Korea Navy chief of naval operations Admiral Kim Kyung-ryul at ROK Navy headquarters on Oct. 12 to discuss opportunities to strengthen bilateral exchanges, naval cooperation and collaboration in the maritime defense industry.

The Navy said the launching of Rajah Humabon reflects its continuing commitment to building a modern and responsive fleet, strengthening strategic partnerships and enhancing its capabilities to protect the country’s maritime interests and uphold national sovereignty in service of the Filipino people.

articles.title: Go seeks review of PSC charter
articles.summary: Sen. Bong Go called for a review of the 36-year-old charter of the Philippine Sports Commission (PSC) to strengthen its capacity to serve Filipino athletes, expand its reach beyond Metro Manila and…

blocks.text: October 19, 2026 | 12:00am
Sen. Bong Go speaks during deliberations on the 2027 budget of the Philippine Sports Commission, at the Senate on Oct. 14.

MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Bong Go called for a review of the 36-year-old charter of the Philippine Sports Commission (PSC) to strengthen its capacity to serve Filipino athletes, expand its reach beyond Metro Manila and respond more effectively to their welfare concerns.

During the Oct. 14 Senate deliberations on the proposed 2027 budget of the PSC, Go said Republic Act 6847, which created the commission in 1990, may already need updating to reflect the present realities of Philippine sports.

PSC Chairman Pato Gregorio told the committee that the existing charter remains technically focused on amateur athletes, creating limitations in situations involving professional players who also represent the country in international competitions.

He said that professional athletes are now allowed to compete in events such as the Olympics and Asian Games, making the distinction increasingly difficult to apply in the context of national-team participation.
Go said Congress should study whether the PSC’s legal mandate and institutional structure remain sufficient.
“This is also important but there is no department that focuses on them… maybe it’s high time to widen your capacity,” Go said.
Go said the immediate priority is to strengthen the PSC itself and expand its presence in the regions so athletes do not have to travel to Metro Manila simply to access government assistance.
The senator said accessibility should be treated as an athlete-welfare issue, noting that transportation costs alone can become an added burden for athletes from far-flung areas.
The hearing also highlighted specific athlete-welfare concerns beyond financial support.
Later in the deliberations, national athlete Kimberly Custodio personally raised issues involving food provisions and nutrition arrangements at the Athletes Village.
Custodio told the committee that some athletes who train outside PSC facilities may not regularly benefit from the meal program and raised concerns about food portions following training.
Go said the larger concern remains ensuring that the government structures responsible for sports are capable of responding to the evolving needs of athletes.
He likewise reiterated support for regional sports facilities and training centers, saying infrastructure and services should be made more accessible outside Metro Manila.
“Let’s make it more accessible for our athletes, our sports facilities,” he added.
Go closed the hearing by reiterating that athlete welfare should remain at the center of government sports policy.

articles.title: Hernando, Inting out of contention for chief justice
articles.summary: Two senior justices of the Supreme Court (SC) were not included in the list of the Judicial and Bar Council (JBC) as nominees to become the next chief justice despite invitations for them to apply.

blocks.text: October 19, 2026 | 12:00am
The logo of the Supreme Court at the Supreme Court Building in Manila.
Philstar.com / Ian Laqui

MANILA, Philippines — Two senior justices of the Supreme Court (SC) were not included in the list of the Judicial and Bar Council (JBC) as nominees to become the next chief justice despite invitations for them to apply.
The names of SC Associate Justices Ramon Paul Hernando and Henri Jean Paul Inting did not appear in the JBC’s list of five SC justices who would undergo public panel interviews in the next two weeks.

Hernando and Inting, along with SC Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen, and Associate Justices Alfredo Benjamin Caguioa and Rodil Zalameda were “invited” by the JBC to apply for the position to be vacated by Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo next month “as a matter of courtesy and in the recognition of their seniority,” according to earlier reports.

The late former president Benigno Aquino III appointed Leonen in November 2012 and Caguioa in January 2016, while former president Rodrigo Duterte chose Hernando in October 2018, Inting in February 2019 and Zalameda in August 2019.

The five candidates for chief justice are Leonen, Caguioa and Zalameda, as well as SC Associate Justices Japar Dimaampao and Jose Midas Marquez. The JBC is set to interview Leonen and Caguioa on Oct. 22, while the rest would be on Oct. 26.
Dimaampao and Marquez were also Duterte appointees in July and September 2021, respectively.

Former vice president and now Naga City Mayor Leni Robredo recommended Leonen to become the next chief justice, while the Bangsamoro Transition Authority Parliament wanted Dimaampao appointed. Marquez secured the endorsements of both retired SC associate justice Arturo Brion and the Association of Retired Regional Trial Court Judges of the Philippines.
Gesmundo is set to retire on Nov. 6 when he reaches the age of 70. President Marcos is expected to choose the replacement within 90 days from retirement.

It would be the President’s third appointment to the SC following Associate Justice Raul Villanueva in June 2025 and his possible choice to take the place of outgoing Associate Justice Amy Lazaro-Javier who will retire on Nov. 16.

articles.title: Oil stockpiling deal eyed between Philippines, United States
articles.summary: The United States, a key actor in the Middle East war that has rattled global fuel supply chains, is now keen to help the Philippines establish its planned strategic petroleum reserves.

blocks.text: October 19, 2026 | 12:00am
Signs reading 'out of stock' are displayed at a gas station amid rising petrol prices in Manila on March 9, 2026.
AFP / Jam Sta Rosa

MANILA, Philippines — The United States, a key actor in the Middle East war that has rattled global fuel supply chains, is now keen to help the Philippines establish its planned strategic petroleum reserves.
Energy Secretary Sharon Garin met with her US counterpart, Chris Wright, on Oct. 15 in Washington to explore ways to expand bilateral energy cooperation between the two countries.

A key item on the meeting was emergency oil stockpiling, with the Philippines exploring opportunities to tap US expertise in building petroleum reserves and preparing for disruptions to global energy supplies.

Garin, who previously pointed to US President Donald Trump’s social media posts as a source of fuel market volatility, said the priority is to ensure “a secure, reliable and affordable energy supply for Filipino families and businesses.”

As a net oil importer, the Philippines quickly felt the impact of tensions between the US and Iran over the strategic Strait of Hormuz, a key shipping route that typically handles about 20 percent of global oil and gas supplies.
The risks have reinforced the Philippines’ push to establish an emergency stockpile of crude oil and refined petroleum products to safeguard domestic fuel supplies during global disruptions.
Beyond oil security, Garin and Wright also discussed cooperation under the landmark “123 agreement,” which provides a framework for the peaceful use of nuclear energy.
The talks also explored opportunities to advance indigenous energy resources, particularly geothermal energy and natural hydrogen.
The US and the Philippines are the world’s largest and third-largest producers of geothermal power, respectively.
Meanwhile, US-based Koloma Inc. holds service contracts for the Philippines’ first natural hydrogen exploration projects.

“Strengthening our partnership with the United States will help us diversify our energy sources, develop indigenous resources and build the technical capabilities needed to support our long-term energy security,” Garin said.
Garin was joined in the US by Philippine Ambassador Jose Manuel Romualdez, National Power Corp. president Jericho Jonas Nograles and Department of Energy director Patrick Aquino.

articles.title: US ambassador to Israel denounces West Bank settler attack on US photojournalist
articles.summary:
Mike Huckabee calls for arrest and prosecution of those responsible as Heidi Levine, 63, recovers in hospital in Israel

The US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, has denounced the settler…

blocks.text: The US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, has denounced the settler attack that left the Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine badly beaten and needing surgery as a “despicable act of terror” and called for the arrest and prosecution of those responsible.

Levine, an award-winning journalist who lives in Israel, was set upon last Friday by masked Israeli settlers who used clubs and other weapons to attack Palestinian people attempting to harvest their olives in occupied West Bank towns.

The 63-year-old photographer, who is in a hospital in Petah Tikva near Tel Aviv recovering from hand surgery, broken ribs and other injuries she sustained in the attack, said she was beaten for more than 10 minutes by the settlers, who also stole her camera, passport and phone.

“I was attacked, pushed to the ground,” Levine said. “Luckily, I had my flak jacket and helmet, otherwise I probably wouldn’t even be here, because they just kept kicking and kicking me.” She added the attack ended when her Palestinian colleagues intervened to save her.

Huckabee, a rightwing ally of President Donald Trump with a track record of hardline, pro-Israel rhetoric, was notably blunt in his condemnation of what he called the “vicious and cowardly attack” on Levine. In a post on X on Saturday, he noted that she was a US citizen who had been clearly identifiable as a journalist.

“We have called for a full investigation, arrest, and prosecution to the fullest extent of the law to whoever participated in this,” Huckabee added. “Attacking a female photographer is despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards. Dishonorable act of senseless violence.”

Israel’s prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, has been ambiguous in addressing Levine’s assault, condemning “violence against anyone” but referring to the attack as “alleged” and saying its circumstances remain unclear.

The attack on the Palestinian farmers and Levine was followed on Saturday by another outbreak of settler violence directed against European diplomats, a French mayor and the archbishop of the French city of Cambrai, who were visiting the occupied West Bank.

Bernard Baudoux, the mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries, was wearing his red, white and blue sash of office and attempting to enter a vehicle with diplomatic plates when he was assaulted and knocked to the ground. A masked militant shouted “Vive la France!” as he launched the attack, a witness said. Badoux’s wife, and Vincent Dollmann, the archbishop of Cambrai, were also threatened by the group of seven men, some armed with clubs.

The group had joined the olive harvest on lands belonging to the Christian town of Taybeh, along with the French consul general in Jerusalem, his wife and other diplomats, and the Belgian and Polish consuls.
“I think that if settlers are behaving like this, there is a tolerance on the part of the Israeli government,” Baudoux told Agence France-Presse after he was attacked.
“The whole world needs to know what’s happening. For me, I’ll go back to my country and everything will be fine. Those who continue to suffer the most are those who are here.”

Violence is surging ahead of bitterly fought elections to be held on 27 October, with Palestinians’ annual olive harvest being repeatedly disrupted by Israeli settlers as Netanyahu seeks to shore up his pro-settlement rightwing base.

France’s foreign minister, Jean-Noël Barrot, has called on Israel to “urgently halt criminal violence” and to arrest those responsible for attacking Baudoux. The EU has condemned the attack and urged “full accountability as well as effective measures to prevent continued acts of violence and violent harassment against Palestinians, including during the ongoing olive harvest season, as well as against journalists”.
The European Commission executive vice-president, Teresa Ribera, went further, posting an interview with Levine in hospital and adding the caption: “They want no witnesses.”
Israel’s foreign ministry has condemned the attack on the diplomats and Israeli police promised to open an investigation.
President Isaac Herzog, who holds a mostly ceremonial role, called Levine in hospital on Saturday, saying the attack was “outrageous and shocking” and was weighing on his conscience.

Netanyahu’s main rival in the elections, the former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, criticised the prime minister over the violence, saying it was “burning away the little legitimacy the state of Israel still possesses”. He described the attacks as “Jewish terrorism, under the auspices of the Israeli government”.

Trump officially endorsed Netanyahu for re-election in a post on his Truth Social network on Sunday, hailing him as “a Great Warrior Prime Minister, and an even greater Partner for Peace in combatting the Islamic Republic of Iran”. He added: “Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself.”
The Washington Post has reiterated its call for a full and transparent investigation into the attack on Levine, even though Israel rarely investigates settler violence fully.
Yesh Din, an Israeli rights group, says around 94% of investigations into settler violence since 2005 have ended without an indictment, with just 3% leading to full or partial convictions.
The Associated Press and Agence France-Presse contributed to this report

articles.title: Police investigate Reform mayor for allegedly sharing ‘naked and sexualised’ images of himself
articles.summary:
Female colleague says she was forced out shortly after incident with Luke Campbell, Hull and East Yorkshire mayor

A Reform UK mayor is under police investigation for allegedly showing…
articles.byline: Josh Halliday North of England editor

blocks.text: A Reform UK mayor is under police investigation for allegedly showing “naked and sexualised” images of himself to a female member of staff.
Luke Campbell, a former Olympic boxing champion and the mayor of Hull and East Yorkshire, is understood to have been questioned under caution by Humberside police earlier this month.
In an incident first reported by the Observer on Sunday, Campbell allegedly showed a senior female colleague four fully naked and sexualised images of himself in May.

The woman said she had felt “shocked, embarrassed and humiliated” and claimed she had been forced out of her job soon after, according to documents submitted as part of an internal grievance procedure at Hull and East Yorkshire combined authority (Heyca).

Campbell, who was elected last May, has not responded to requests to comment. It is understood that he has not been arrested in relation to the allegations, which Reform UK has said he “firmly denies”.

blocks.caption: Luke Campbell, pictured in 2012, won gold at the London Olympics. Photograph: Gary Calton/The Guardian

blocks.text: A Reform UK spokesperson said: “Luke firmly denies the allegations. They come from a disgruntled employee attempting to leverage a settlement in a meritless workplace dispute.”
The allegations against Campbell came to light after a year-long ITV investigation uncovered racist comments from a number of Reform UK councillors and a prospective MP.

An aspiring Reform UK MP was suspended after telling an undercover reporter that Muslims could not be British and asylum seekers crossing the English channel should be put in “concentration camps”, in footage due to be broadcast on Sunday night.
Nigel Farage’s party said it had opened investigations where activists or members had “clearly behaved inappropriately”, adding that there was “no room for racism” in the party.

Nadine Dorries, a former Conservative minister and now a Reform UK member, came to Campbell’s defence on Sunday by claiming that the “sexualised” image was in fact a 2013 magazine cover showing the former boxer posing naked from the waist up after he won gold at the 2012 London Olympics.
However, that appears to be at odds with witness testimony submitted as part of an internal grievance procedure at Heyca, where Campbell is mayor.

In one document, corroborated by the Guardian, a senior female colleague said Campbell had called her over to a computer screen, where she was shown “several naked and sexualised images” of the mayor.
after newsletter promotion
A separate witness said they saw a naked man with a tattoo in one of the images, whereas no tattoo is visible on the magazine front cover.

The main complainant said in a witness statement: “I was deliberately exposed to naked and sexualised images involving the mayor in the workplace, without my consent, and was laughed at when I was visibly embarrassed.
“In my view, this was unwanted conduct of a sexual nature which violated my dignity and created a humiliating, degrading and offensive working environment.”

About three weeks after the alleged incident, the female officer, who was working as a contractor but had accepted the offer of a permanent role, was allegedly told on a Teams call that the offer had been withdrawn.

In a separate document, a second colleague said they had felt “uneasy” after allegedly seeing Campbell and two male colleagues ushering over a female officer to look at his laptop, which showed an image of a naked man with a tattoo.
The Guardian understands that this second employee recalled comments then being made about Campbell’s tattoo and that they saw the mayor lift his shirt to show the tattoo.

A spokesperson for Heyca confirmed to the Observer that a police investigation was under way. He said: “As with all public authorities, the combined authority has a standards process that can be engaged to deal with complaints about members and a complaints procedure that can be used to deal with complaints about officers.
“The standards process and the complaints procedure must be carried out in a fair and independent manner.”
Humberside police has been contacted for comment.

articles.title: French government in crisis talks after ‘colossal failure of the state’
articles.summary:
Ministers, officials and police under pressure over response to days of violent unrest in cities across France

The French government was in crisis talks on Sunday after one of the most…

blocks.text: The French government was in crisis talks on Sunday after one of the most violent days of unrest in years left public buildings burned, hundreds of shops destroyed and looted, and more than 2000 people arrested in cities across the country.

Politicians on the left and right called for the resignation of the interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, after the government appeared to have been caught by surprise by the scale of violence as state buildings were stormed and torched, bus stops smashed, roads barricaded and shops broken into and destroyed.
The president, Emmanuel Macron, who is standing down next spring, was preparing to address the nation on Sunday night. He wrote on social media there was “no place for violence” in France.

blocks.caption: A car burns in a Paris street near graffiti reading ‘introduction to civil war’. Photograph: Guillaume Saligot/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Police and officials faced challenges of different types on Saturday. First, tens of thousands of peaceful protesters attended calm marches through major cities including Paris, supporting schoolchildren’s demands for more teachers and repairs to decrepit schools. Those marches, which came after four weeks of street marches and barricades of schools, were attended by parents, teachers and grandparents as well as students and workers protesting over the high cost of living. The demonstrators carried banners saying the government was not listening to them and calling for more money for public services.

But separately to those peaceful demonstrations, different groups caught police and officials by surprise with moving gatherings, sporadic burning, the barricading of streets and clashing with police in cities including Paris, Bordeaux, Nice and Marseille.

blocks.caption: A protester throws a smoke flare towards gendarmes in Bordeaux, south-western France. Photograph: Christophe Archambault/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Finally, masked looters took advantage of what French media called the “chaos” on the streets to smash shopfronts and grab goods. In Paris, groups of looters, some of whom appeared to be children, were seen running through the night with clothes and shoeboxes after masked adult men smashed shopfronts.

In Paris, where police said a record 855 people had been arrested, the burnt-out remains of barricades built using bikes, bins and other materials littered streets on Sunday. Several streets had smashed shop windows and the remains of torched cars. The capital had experienced “a level of violence that we have never seen before, I believe”, said the Socialist deputy mayor, Lamia El Aaraje.

blocks.caption: Burnt-out cars, smashed windows and the remains of barricades littered the streets of Paris on Sunday.  Photograph: Stéphanie Lecocq/Reuters

blocks.text: In Limoges in central France, where the 19th-century town hall was burned down, the mayor, Guillaume Guérin, said the people who stormed his building “were not demonstrators that defend causes” but “people organised for war”. He said those who stormed and torched the town hall had told a building caretaker he would be killed, and told elected officials they would “burn”. He said there had been a failure of the state to deal with the crisis.

“Around 3:30pm our municipal police, although present in number, found themselves no longer able to fight against the violence of rioters because they had run out of munition,” Guérin said. He called this “a colossal failure of the state”.

blocks.caption: The mayor of Marseille, where masked groups stormed the city hall and a police station, said questions must be asked about policing tactics.  Photograph: Sener Yilmaz Aslan/Getty Images

blocks.text: In Marseille, where masked groups stormed the city hall and a police station, the Socialist mayor, Benoît Payan, told BFMTV: “I have no words … I never thought I’d ever live through something like this. Hordes of rioters and looters attacked our common [state] buildings … with no real demands, but with the sole aim to wreck the demands of those who had demonstrated legitimately.”
Payan said questions must be asked about policing tactics, as other town hall buildings, for example in Lille, were also targeted.
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: Protesters arrive to force entry into the town hall in Lille, northern France. Photograph: Sameer Al-Doumy/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Grégory Doucet, the Green mayor of Lyon, said he had never seen such violence in his city, including the torching of the historic tourist office. He told Le Monde: “I’m stunned by the violence against public and state property. I saw and heard fear and anger. Shop-owners felt abandoned.”

Doucet said the government must find a “sense of nuance” in properly examining what happened and “avoiding stereotypes”. He said the government needed to give a political response to long-running societal demands from peaceful demonstrators on one hand, and also examine roots of violence.

Traders’ unions said over 1,500 shops and businesses had been ransacked with a cost running into tens of millions of euros. “This had nothing to do with the peaceful protesters,” said one shoe-shop owner in Paris. “These were organised groups who were breaking things and looting. We’d never seen anything like it.”

blocks.caption: A protester wrapped in a French national flag stands in front of Lyon’s burning tourism office. Photograph: Jeff Pachoud/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Opposition politicians questioned the government’s policing tactics, saying there had been a lack of state intelligence.

The interior ministry said there had been more than 2,000 arrests and about 600 police, firefighters and paramedics had been hurt. A 17-year-old boy had his right hand blown off by a crowd-control grenade in the southern city of Saint-Étienne.

Macron’s centrist government and the far-right frontrunner for the presidential election, Marine Le Pen, both blamed what they called “ultra-left” groups for the violence. The prime minister, Sébastien Lecornu, said the government would not be “intimidated” by ⁠violence, and blamed the unrest on the “ultra-left” and criminals.

The radical-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon, who attended the peaceful street demonstration in Paris on Saturday, accused the government of organisational failings that had “opened the door to chaos”.
Lecornu replied on social media: “Laying the responsibility for violence on heads of police is a dangerous and cynical reversal of responsibilities.”

articles.title: Scholars conclude ‘beyond doubt’ that Shakespeare was main author of Edward III
articles.summary:
Exclusive: Play anonymously published in 1596 was collaboration between Shakespeare and Christopher Marlowe, according to computer analysis

Dramatic new evidence concludes that the play…

blocks.text: Dramatic new evidence concludes that the play Edward III should be added to William Shakespeare’s canon, and also that it was a major collaboration with his contemporary rival Christopher Marlowe.

The history was published anonymously in 1596, and it has long been thought that Shakespeare wrote at least a few scenes. However, Dr Rory Loughnane, a leading scholar and co-author of the research, told the Guardian that computerised textual analysis pushed the case “beyond any reasonable doubt” that the Stratford-born playwright was the principal writer.

He said: “That’s the new finding, that both Shakespeare, now confirmed beyond doubt, and Marlowe, unexpectedly found for the first time, are present in the play, and therefore it represents a newly found collaboration between the two.

“It has massive implications for our understanding of the relationship between the two most important dramatists of this period. This changes both the Shakespeare canon and the Marlowe canon and will be of significant international interest.”

blocks.caption: A portrait of William Shakespeare from the title page of the 1623 first folio. Illustration: GraphicaArtis/Getty Images

blocks.text: Loughnane, a reader in early modern studies at the University of Kent and general editor of the Oxford Marlowe editorial project, collaborated on the study with Brett Greatley-Hirsch, a professor of renaissance literature and textual studies at the University of Leeds.

Edward III did not appear in the 1623 first folio collection of Shakespeare’s plays. Loughnane edited it for the 2016 New Oxford Shakespeare: Complete Works, acknowledging that a couple of scenes had probably been written by him, and the play had also appeared in a 2005 volume. Loughnane also co-authored the Canon and Chronology study in the New Oxford Shakespeare: Authorship Companion, which made the case for Shakespeare’s part-authorship, but acknowledged a need for further research.
Loughnane said: “Our new research suggests that Marlowe is Shakespeare’s collaborator on Edward III. This is the first time this case has been made seriously.”

The researchers used various forms of computerised linguistic analysis in comparing Edward III with securely attributed works by 10 dramatists active between the late 1580s and the mid-1590s. In one test, 23 segments – “the lion’s share” – were identified as being written by Shakespeare, while nine segments were classified as Marlowe, whose works include Doctor Faustus.

Loughnane said these findings were particularly significant because a 2016 study had found that Marlowe was a co-author of Shakespeare’s three Henry VI plays: “Their collaboration on Edward III in 1592 suggests a more sustained writing relationship in their mid-to-late 20s.”

Marlowe died aged just 29, after a brawl in a lodging house in 1593. “We have become accustomed to thinking of Marlowe and Shakespeare as rivals – two outstanding authors, born within a few weeks of one another, making their names in the same theatrical world of the late 1580s and early 1590s,” Loughnane said. “But we now know that their relationship was much more complicated than that. They were not simply rivals or influences on one another.”

blocks.caption: A portrait thought to be of Christopher Marlowe. Photograph: Pictures from History/Universal Images Group/Getty Images

blocks.text: Rather than attributing particular lines to either author, the study focused on linguistic features and the distribution of certain “marker” words, such as “martial”, which are typically present in Marlowe’s plays and correspondingly atypical in the plays of other dramatists. They also suggest Shakespeare’s authorship of segments, “which may overlap with bits of writing he did not do”, and Marlowe’s authorship of other segments.

The analysis confirms that a speech from the beginning of scene 13 was written by Shakespeare, when a sudden and ominous darkening of the sky causes fear in the French camp, and King Jean says: “A sudden darkness hath defaced the sky …”
The analysis concludes that a speech from the final scene of the play was written by Marlowe: “Great servitor to bloody Mars in arms, / The Frenchman’s terror and his country’s fame.”

Greatley-Hirsch said: “What makes the evidence particularly compelling is that we’re not relying on a single verbal parallel or statistical test. Different forms of analysis, looking at different features of the language, appear to repeatedly distinguish Marlowe’s writing from Shakespeare’s within the play.”

The research will be published in the Shakespeare Quarterly later this year. Insights into Shakespeare’s early career are also explored in Loughnane’s forthcoming book, Shakespeare at Thirty, to be published by Princeton University Press this week.

Loughnane has also curated an exhibition about the life and times of Marlowe in the playwright’s native Canterbury. The Making of Marlowe runs until 22 November at the Beaney House of Art & Knowledge.

articles.title: Six-year-old among two dead after Kansas woman drives through soccer game, with 11 more injured
articles.summary:
Wichita police say 34-year-old truck driver from Garden City was taken into custody amid case at youth soccer game

The two people
articles.byline: Maya Yang and Ramon Antonio Vargas

blocks.text: The two people killed on Saturday when a truck drove through a youth soccer game in north-east Wichita, Kansas, were a six-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man, according to authorities.
Eleven other people between the ages of five and 68 were injured in a case whose possible motivations remained unclear early on Sunday, by when it had captured attention across the US.

In a news briefing updating initial information, Wichita police said the driver at the center of the case was a 34-year-old woman from Garden City, Kansas, which is about three and a half hours away by car.
Authorities did not immediately release her name any of the victims’ names, including the two killed.
Police said they took the driver into custody after she drove through a field at Stryker Sports Complex during a youth soccer game at about 3.30pm on Saturday.

When police and paramedics arrived in response to emergency calls, they found the truck on the west field of the complex. Two juveniles were inside the truck with the driver, Wichita police captain, Aaron Moses, told news media.
The woman has a valid driver’s license and no outstanding warrants, Moses said.
The boy and man who were killed were both from McPherson, Kansas, about an hour drive north of Wichita. Police said the victims were not related.
Ten of those injured had serious but not life-threatening injuries, police said. Those included children aged five, eight and nine – as well as adults between 28 and 68 years old.
The 11th person reported as injured was a 61-year-old woman who had nontraumatic medical issues, police said.
The competitive youth soccer club McPherson City FC said in a Facebook post on Saturday that it had “suffered an unimaginable tragedy at Stryker Soccer Complex”.

blocks.caption: Police attend the scene where a vehicle drove through a soccer game at the Stryker Sports Complex in Wichita, Kansas, on Saturday in a still image from video. Photograph: ABC Affiliate KAKE/Reuters

blocks.text: “We ask that you keep all those involved in your thoughts and prayers,” the club’s post continued. “Dealing with a loss of this magnitude also calls for privacy and respect for all our soccer community. Please allow time for healing and grieving to take place and be there for those that seek guidance.”
After saying that McPherson City FC would later post further information in regards to the club and its upcoming events, the post concluded: “Please hold your loved ones tight tonight.”
McPherson’s municipal government wrote in a separate Facebook post: “Our community is hurting, and we stand together, and in support.”
“Stay strong, McPherson,” that post also said. “Be there [and] be kind.”
Stryker Sports Complex announced that all events had been cancelled there until further notice.

“We ask that you keep all individuals and families affected in your thoughts and prayers during this difficult time,” the complex also said in its announcement. “Please avoid the complex to allow emergency personnel to carry out their work.
“Updates regarding future events will be shared as information becomes available.”
Meanwhile, the Kansas State High School Activities Association also suspended its third-place and championship flag football games, which had been scheduled for later on Saturday at the complex.

blocks.caption: A stretcher is brought to the scene at the Stryker Sports Complex in Wichita, Kansas, on Saturday in a still image from video.  Photograph: ABC Affiliate KAKE/Reuters

blocks.text: “The KSHSAA extends our condolences to the families and teams [affected] by the incident,” the association said.
The organization said it planned on providing details about rescheduled games on Monday.
Saturday marked the second time in less than 26 years that the athletic complex near the corner of North Greenwich Road and East 29th Street was at the center of a high-profile, deadly case.

Brothers named Jonathan and Reginald Carr were convicted of shooting five people – including four fatally – on a snow-covered field there in December 2000 during a crime spree that also involved robbery, rape and torture, according to information culled from court filings and media reports.

The Carrs were sentenced to die over what some have referred to as the “Wichita massacre”. And in July, Kansas governor Laura Kelly denied their requests for their death sentences to be commuted to life imprisonment.

articles.title: Manchester City owner’s £55m housing loan while Burnham was mayor investigated
articles.summary:
Scrutiny committee looks into financing of Manchester Life project as PM promises ‘full transparency’

A £55m loan to Manchester City’s Abu Dhabi owner will be investigated as part of a…
articles.byline: Josh Halliday North of England editor

blocks.text: A £55m loan to Manchester City’s Abu Dhabi owner will be investigated as part of a review into a fund for housing projects while Andy Burnham was mayor.

The prime minister has faced weeks of scrutiny over his links to Manchester City’s super-rich owners after the club was found guilty of boosting its income by £900m in a nine-year breach of financial rules.

Burnham, the former Greater Manchester mayor, was accused of siding with the Abu Dhabi owners after the “unprecedented” rule breach, when he said they had been “such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester” and that he would be “really concerned” to lose them from the sport.
He could now face more uncomfortable questions after councillors in Greater Manchester said they planned to investigate loans made to property companies while he was mayor.

In 2017, three companies ultimately controlled by the Manchester City owner, Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan, the vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates, were loaned £55m as part of a fund operated by Burnham’s Greater Manchester combined authority (GMCA).

blocks.caption: Manchester City owner, Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan, seen here in 2010, is also deputy PM of the UAE. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters

blocks.text: The loans were to help finance a major housing development called Manchester Life, which promised to create 6,000 homes in an “unprecedented” opportunity for the city. GMCA said the loans had been repaid in full but has not disclosed the interest rate or why Sheikh Mansour, as a scion of one of the world’s wealthiest families, would have been eligible.

It emerged last week that Burnham had met City’s owners while enjoying hospitality from the club at its Etihad Stadium weeks before the loans were approved. That meeting later disappeared from public records before it came to light last week, prompting the prime minister to ask GMCA to carry out a “manual trawl” of his meetings to ensure “full transparency”.

John Leech, a Liberal Democrat councillor in Manchester, said the fund – which has handed out £1bn to 50 separate developers since 2015 – would be investigated by GMCA’s overview and scrutiny committee, which he chairs.
Leech told the BBC the approval process for loans had been criticised as “very opaque in the past and that it’s not necessarily been clearly understood why X was successful and Y wasn’t”.
after newsletter promotion

He said it was “not unreasonable” to ask why seemingly successful businesses needed to borrow public money through this loan scheme. “In the case of Abu Dhabi, you would imagine that they wouldn’t have any problem accessing funds from elsewhere as well,” he said.
“And so the process clearly does seem to be out of kilter with what the original stated aims were back in 2015.”
He added: “We just want to be clear that there is a transparent rather than an opaque process”.

Downing Street declined to comment. A GMCA spokesperson said it was supporting Leech’s overview and scrutiny committee with its inquiries. They said the fund had built 11,000 new homes and was contributing “billions of pounds worth of development at no cost to the taxpayer”.
GMCA added: “Decisions to grant loans from the fund are taken publicly. Not a single viable scheme was ever turned down and funds were lent to around 50 different developers.

“The fund is open to all developers, with lending criteria based on parameters set by the government and developed with external financial experts to reflect due diligence standards in the private sector.”

Ukraine used more than 1,000 drones to target Russian oil depots, logistics facilities and datacentres

Two people have been killed and at least 17 injured as Russia and Ukraine continue to…

blocks.text: Two people have been killed and at least 17 injured as Russia and Ukraine continue to trade strikes on each other’s power infrastructure, after the breakdown of Donald Trump’s short-lived and unilaterally declared “energy ceasefire”.

One person was killed and 15 wounded overnight after Ukraine used more than 1,000 drones to target Russian oil depots, logistics facilities and datacentres in one of its largest ever aerial bombardments.

St Petersburg’s governor, Alexander Beglov, said on Sunday that fires ⁠had broken out overnight at the city’s oil terminal, ​an oil depot and industrial ‌warehouses. A logistics centre belonging to the Russian retailer Ozon and a datacentre for the local tech company VK were also targeted, both companies confirmed.

Alexander Drozdenko, the governor of the Leningrad region that surrounds St Petersburg, said 145 drones had been shot down and about 20,000 people were without electricity after the raid. “A large-scale [unmanned aerial vehicle] attack continues to be repelled,” he wrote on Telegram.

blocks.caption: Smoke billows into the sky after Ukrainian drone strikes on an industrial zone in St Petersburg.  Photograph: AP

blocks.text: Meanwhile, local officials in the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia said Russian strikes had killed a woman and wounded at least two other people, including a six-year-old girl. Two apartment buildings, 18 cars and an educational institution had been damaged by the attack, according to Mykhailo Semikin, the head of the Zaporizhzhia regional military administration.
Tensions are deepening between Kyiv and Washington, with the US president criticising Ukraine for its strikes on Russian oil infrastructure, despite continued Russian aggression.

Trump announced an “energy ceasefire” last week – which neither side said they agreed to beforehand – that quickly collapsed as Moscow continued its strikes on Ukraine’s power grid and Kyiv eventually resumed its hits on Russian oil refineries.

The Russian defence ministry said its air defence units had downed 1,015 Ukrainian drones around the country overnight. The Tass news agency quoted the ​Kremlin ​spokesperson, Dmitry Peskov, who said Russia was responding with systematic, large-scale ⁠strikes.
“The Kyiv ​regime is resisting, but this cannot ​change the course ‌of events,” he ​said, ​answering a question about how Russia might respond to Kyiv’s attack on St Petersburg.

On Saturday, Russia said it had carried out a major overnight attack, targeting Ukraine’s largest steelworks in the city of Kryvyi Rih and ⁠vessels using the port of Odesa. In a ‌statement, Russia’s defence ministry said its forces had also hit an electricity substation in the north-western city of Zhytomyr and another steel ‌plant in Zaporizhzhia.

blocks.caption: A house damaged by a Russian airstrike in the frontline city of Sloviansk in eastern Ukraine.  Photograph: State Emergency Service Of Ukraine/Reuters

blocks.text: In the Trump administration’s latest effort to reduce tensions with Russia, the US president announced on Friday that he would put a hold on a sweeping new sanctions package targeting the Russian economy, telling Congress the pause on the legislation passed by both chambers was in the national interest.
Trump has yet to give details about what he has decided regarding further sanctions on Russia.

“We’ll figure it out, and you’ll figure it out,” he told reporters at a fundraising dinner at his Florida estate on Saturday. “But it’s a very good decision, and it’s going to be a decision that’s good for the country, and I think good for the world.”
In a post on X on Sunday, Zelenskyy said in the week since Trump’s announcement of an energy ceasefire Russia had attacked Ukraine’s energy, oil and gas sectors 76 times.

He also said that the previous night alone, energy facilities in four Ukrainian regions had been attacked and tens of thousands of families were still without power. He accused Russia of trying to cause a blackout.
after newsletter promotion

“America should see that Russia is not taking any reciprocal steps in response to sanctions relief or agreements,” he said. “On the contrary, they take every signal of an opportunity to make money as proof that their bet on war is paying off and they can keep fighting.”

Zelenskyy also stressed that the war was continuing due to Russia’s invasion – not because Ukraine was defending itself. “It is Russia that must face pressure for peace to have a chance. Thank you to everyone who understands this and helps,” he said.

Fears that the conflict could be spilling over into Nato’s borders were stoked again on Sunday morning after Lithuania told residents in central and ⁠northern parts of the country to seek shelter for about an hour after an unidentified flying object entered its ⁠airspace.
During the red alert, Nato fighter jets were ‌scrambled to the area, and Kaunas airport, near Lithuania’s second largest city, was temporarily closed, the national crisis management centre said.
The Nato aircraft were unable to visually identify the object due to cloudy weather and did not attempt to shoot it down, the centre said.
Ukraine’s foreign ministry later said ⁠it regretted the possible diversion of its ⁠drones into ⁠Lithuanian airspace ​on Sunday, which it said may ⁠have been caused by Russian electronic warfare.

“We apologise for any ​disruption, risks and concern this may have caused,” a spokesperson, ‌Heorhii Tykhyi, wrote on X. “We are committed to ⁠sharing all relevant information with ​our ​Lithuanian partners to ​establish the full circumstances ​of ‌the incident.“

Ukrainian drones have repeatedly entered Nato airspace in the ​Baltic region in ‌recent months. Kyiv ​has said they ​were steered off course by Russian signal jamming. Such incidents have stoked concerns that Russia’s war in Ukraine could spread.
Reuters, the Associated Press and Agence France-Presse contributed to this report

articles.title: Ukraine apologizes after a suspected drone crashes in Lithuania, damaging a moving car.
articles.summary: Debris has damaged a moving car in Lithuania, where NATO jets were scrambled. Kyiv says Russian jamming may have diverted drones targeting Russia.

image.caption: Italian Eurofighters operating under NATO command were scrambled in response to the drone incident in Lithuania (FILE 04/03/2024)Image: Armando Babani/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Ukraine apologized Sunday after a suspected drone crashed in northern Lithuania, prompting shelter warnings and the deployment of NATO fighter jets.
The incident raised fresh concerns about the spillover of Russia's war against Ukraine into NATO territory, although the drone's origin and whether it carried explosives remained under investigation.
What happened in Lithuania?
Lithuanian authorities told residents in central and northern regions to seek shelter Sunday morning after detecting an unidentified flying object.
Debris damaged a moving civilian vehicle, but no one was injured, national crisis management centre chief Vilmantas Vitkauskas told Lithuanian radio.
Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas said the drone probably entered from neighboring Poland. He proposed a joint investigation with Warsaw.
Two Italian Eurofighter jets operating under NATO command were deployed, a NATO spokesperson said. Kaunas said weather conditions prevented visual identification.
Have similar incidents happened before?
Lithuania and its Baltic neighbors have experienced several drone incursions during the war.
Ukrainian drones intended to strike targets in northwestern Russia have previously strayed into Baltic airspace and crashed. Russian-made drones have also entered Lithuania from Belarus.
Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda described Sunday's incident as another example of the war spilling onto NATO's eastern flank.

articles.title: Pope appears in public for first time since surgery
articles.summary: After undergoing a lung operation, the pope said he will resume his duties gradually. There is no "clinical reason" for his South America trip not to go ahead, his surgeon said.

image.caption: The pope looked physically well as he addressed the crowdsImage: Alessandra Tarantino/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Pope Leo XIV said he would resume his duties "gradually" as he addressed the crowd for the first time since his lung cancer surgery.
Part of the pope's right lung was removed as part of the operation, which took place at the Gemelli Hospital in Rome. He was discharged on Saturday.

The Catholic leader thanked those who prayed for him while he was hospitalized, saying he would "gradually assume" his activities as the crowd cheered upon seeing him appearing. The 71-year-old spoke normally and looked physically well.
The people said the "delicate phase" is behind him, thanking "God and your prayers" for it and also expressing his gratitude to the medical staff at the Rome hospital.

During his time at hospital, the pope still made his worries about the Ukrainian civilian population clear. He held a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin, urging for a ceasefire in the Ukrainian town of Oleshky, located on the front line.
Putin reacted by saying Ukraine is responsible for the situation.
Recovery in ten days
According to his surgeon, the pontiff is in an "absolutely satisfactory clinical condition," with his full recovery probably taking some ten days.

blocks.caption: The crowds cheered as the pope made his first appearance Image: Gregorio Borgia/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: "His determination to achieve a very quick and very effective recovery from every point of view was really commendable," Dr. Stefano Margaritora told Vatican News.
Margaritora said the tumor had been found during a routine X-ray checkup, while also saying the operation to remove it was "routine."

The pope's next major assignment would be his trip to South America, in which visits to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru are planned. The trip should take place between November 6 and 17. Speaking about the pope's recovery, Dr. Margaritora said he sees "no clinical reason" why the trip should be called off.
Testing of the tumor and related lymph nodes was underway, with the results determining whether Pope Leo needs additional medical treatment.
The 71-year-old Pope Leo was born in Chicago. He's been in his role since May 2025.
